• He came to India in the** 7th century** and stayed here for **14 years**, during which he** travelled extensively **and wrote about his experiences in his book **"The Great Tang Records on the Western Regions".**
 
• Hsuan Tsang was a **Buddhist monk** and his main purpose of visiting India was to study **Buddhism and collect Buddhist texts.**
 
• He visited many important Buddhist sites in India, including** Bodh Gaya, **where he meditated under the **Bodhi tree** and studied Buddhist philosophy under the guidance of a famous **Indian monk, Shilabhadra.**

• **Faxian** was a **Chinese Buddhist monk** who visited India in the **5th century.**
 
• **Etsing **is** not** a known Chinese traveller, and** Ibn Battuta **was a** Moroccan explorer** who visited India in the **14th century.**
 
• Hence, the **correct **answer is option 1.

questions.question: Which is the only living representative of Sphenopsida that has an underground, creeping and perennial rhizome that gives off aerial as well as underground branches?

• Equisetum has an **underground, creeping and perennial rhizome** that gives off **aerial **as well as** underground branches**.
 
• It is the only living representative of **Sphenopsida**, a group of **vascular plants **that were dominant during the **Carboniferous period.**
 
• **Adiantum**, also known as** maidenhair fern,** belongs to the group of **ferns **and **does no**t have an underground rhizome.
 
 
• It has **delicate fronds** and is commonly grown as an** ornamental plant.**
 
 
 
• **Dryopteris** is another **group of ferns** that **does not** have an underground rhizome.
 
 
• It is commonly known as **wood fern **and is also grown as an **ornamental plant.**
 
 
 
• **Selaginella, **also known as **spike moss,** is a group of plants that are **similar to ferns** but have** smaller leaves** and are adapted to grow in** dry environments.**
 
 
• They **do not** have an underground rhizome.

• **Adiantum** is also used in **traditional medicine** to treat **respiratory and digestive problems.**
 
 
• It is also used in **hair care products** because of its **high silica content.**

• **Trichloromethane** is better known as **Chloroform.**
 
• Chloroform is a **colorless liquid** with a **sweet odor** and a **nonflammable nature.**
 
• It is commonly used as an **anesthetic during surgeries** and medical procedures.
 
• Chloroform was also used as a** solvent **and in the production of** refrigerants and pesticides**.
 
• However, its use has been restricted due to its** potential toxicity** and **carcinogenic effects**.

• They are also used as **propellants** in **aerosol sprays** and as a **refrigerant.**
 
• However, they are **highly flammable** and can pose a **fire hazard** if not handled properly.
 
 
 
• **LPG**
 
 
• LPG or liquefied petroleum gas is a mixture of **propane and butane.**
 
• It is commonly used as fuel for **heating, cooking, and transportation.**
 
• LPG is a** clean-burning fuel** and emits **fewer pollutants **compared to other fossil fuels.
 
• However, it is** highly flammable **and can **pose safety risks **if not handled properly.

• Nitrous oxide has a **euphoric effect **and can cause **laughing and giggling**, hence the name.
 
• However, it can also cause** dizziness, nausea, **and in rare cases,** loss of consciousness.**

• The concept of Fundamental Duties was inspired by the **Constitution of the Soviet Union.**
 
• The Fundamental Duties were added to the Constitution on the recommendation of the** Swaran Singh Committee.**
